items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: So I knew a girl in Chicago by the name of Ellen Winston. Her mother and my mother knew each other.

ctx.x: Her name was Miss Florida Edgerton. Florida Cummings was her name. I didn't know her name was Edgerton till later years. And I didn't know that the gentleman that was beside her was her husband, you know. But I know that I got on with the lady and the gentleman. The school teacher, my school teacher was the one I was interested in. And I got off the streetcar -- Lord, have mercy. Sometimes I think about that. I got off the streetcar and left them on the streetcar, but when I got off, like I'm -- I was facing this…

is her Sunday off." And I said, "Well, will you please, ma'am, let me stay here till she comes?" And she said yes. And she said, "Honey, what are you doing here? Where are you from?" And I said, "Well, --" I told her I was from Memphis, you know, and she said, "You are? Does your mother know where you are?" And I said, "No, ma'am." So she said, "Well, you just sit down," and she said, "Are you hungry," you know, and I said, "No, ma'am." I was too glad that that was where Helen lived, you know. So I sat there, and…
